paragraphs.text: Only 10 events are documented here, along with 49 people and places, and some locations in this account are approximate.
Sejong the Great, creator of Hangul, was born here in 1397, and Yi Sun-sin, a Korean admiral, in 1545.
The Imjin War, two Japanese invasions of Korea, ran from 1592 CE to 1598 CE and ended with the withdrawal of Japanese forces after a military stalemate in Korea's southern provinces.
Gojong of the Korean Empire was born here in 1852.
In 1882 soldiers of the Joseon Army began the Imo Incident, an uprising in Seoul.
Korea negotiated treaties with the United Kingdom in 1883, Russia in 1884 and Japan in 1885.
The Donghak Peasant Revolution took place in Korea from 1894 CE to 1895 CE.
On 23 July 1894, during its ceasefire, Imperial Japanese forces occupied Gyeongbokgung palace to establish a pro-Japanese government.
On 8 October 1895, Queen Min, the consort of Gojong, was assassinated by Japanese agents at the royal palace Gyeongbokgung in Seoul.
The Eulsa Treaty of 1905 made Korea a protectorate of Imperial Japan.
On August 1, 1907, in reaction to its disbandment, the Korean army rebelled against Japanese forces at the Namdaemun Gate in Seoul and was suppressed.
